newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First decision likely to disappoint-Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ First decision likely to disappoint-Peters.

text.p: New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters told a political rally on Sunday his party would disappoint a significant number of people whoever it decided to team up with after October 12's inconclusive election.
Peters also told a meeting of about 600 supporters at his home base of Tauranga that NZ First would soon decide on who it would form a coalition with.
NZ First, which went to the polls on a nationalist platform, has been in talks with the centre right National Party and the centre left Labour Party since the election.
Despite polling third after National and Labour, NZ First holds the balance of power as to what form the new government will take.
"It's an awesome responsibility, and we're here to report today that we're almost there," Peters said.
"When it happens I ask that you give it a chance and don't make your minds up until we've had three years to make it work," Peters said.

The party did not expect to get everything it wanted from the coalition talks, adding it was inevitable that a significant number of supporters and New Zealanders in general would be disappointed at the outcome.

"What NZ First gains in the negotiations should not be seen as someone else's loss. We won't get everything we want, but unless we are part of the government we won't get anything at all," Peters told a news conference after the meeting.
"No matter which way we go, we're still going to disappoint a significant proportion of supporters and New Zealanders generally," Peters said. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
